currentContext.strengths: Legacy spanning over eight decades as a household FMEG name and vital pillar of the Bajaj Group|Pan-India distribution scale: 850+ distributors (Board's overview) / 2,000+ channel partners (MD&CEO message), nearly 2,00,000+ retail outlets, and 770+/778 consumer care centres reaching 19,000 pin codes|Multi-brand 'house of brands' portfolio (Bajaj, Morphy Richards, Nirlep) each anchored in a distinct value proposition, spanning the full price spectrum|Full brand ownership of Morphy Richards (post-acquisition) enabling sharper premiumisation and margin control versus the prior licensing arrangement|Engineering depth in professional lighting projects (smart cities, stadiums, industrial complexes, tunnels) described by the MD & CEO as a real competitive moat|Digital enablement across the trade network (DMS, Sarathi App, DSO App, Power BI) strengthening distributor governance and transparency
currentContext.strategies: Accelerating domestic sourcing, localising critical components, and reducing single-country dependencies in response to tariff and geopolitical supply-chain risk.|Operating a clear two-brand strategy: the BAJAJ brand (refreshed identity) serves mass and aspirational segments, while the fully-owned Morphy Richards addresses the upper mid-market and premium lifestyle segment.|Accelerating premiumisation — launching upgraded, energy-efficient and higher-value SKUs (400+ new SKUs across consumer products and lighting in recent years) and moving the product mix upward while defending category-leading positions (No.1 in mixer-grinders, No.2 in water heaters).|Deepening distribution quality over mere distribution width, alongside continued expansion of channel reach into underserved and rural markets.|Deliberate inventory correction in the Consumer Products business carried out through H1 and Q3 FY26 with channel partners, to establish a cleaner, healthier inventory base for more disciplined, sustainable growth from Q4 FY26 onwards.|Driving execution rigour and cost/working-capital efficiency across the business (supply chain, sales, service) through lean initiatives and digital tools to improve inventory turns and optimise cost structure.|Investing in future-ready capabilities: strengthening the digital backbone, data analytics for demand forecasting, and accelerating e-commerce/omnichannel presence.|Foray into Solar, Switchgear and Wires categories, adjacent to the existing distribution network and aligned with the government's housing and electrification agenda.|Partnership with TIH Foundation for smart lighting solutions for smart cities, reflecting an ambition to move from selling products to solving for integrated environments.|Sustainability positioned as embedded operating practice (not an add-on), with continued BRSR-framework disclosure and greater granularity on environmental performance.|Dividend for the year is recommended by the Board and, per the AGM notice resolution, is paid out of the Company's free reserves; the Board's practice (evidenced elsewhere in this AR bundle) has been to maintain the per-share dividend even in a loss-making year as a signal of continued commitment to shareholders. This bundle does not carry the narrative text of a separately articulated Dividend Distribution Policy beyond the AGM resolution language.
currentContext.expansion: The Company forayed into the switchgear segment with the launch of the BAJAJ SECURA brand (switchgear and wires), described as a strategic expansion of the lighting solutions business that extends the Company's generational expertise into a new category. The Company broadened its international footprint in FY2026 through targeted market initiatives: in Sri Lanka it introduced new appliance categories and strengthened the Morphy Richards presence through its established partner; in Nepal it implemented DMDC-based distribution for ceiling fans while consolidating appliance sales; in Dubai efforts focused on re-export partners with a consistent monthly push to grow market share in the ceiling fan segment. Looking to FY2027, the Professional Lighting business plans to strengthen its competitive edge through R&D and digital integration, with an emphasis on ultra-efficient solutions that reduce carbon footprints; growth efforts will be pursued across infrastructure, sports, office spaces and data centres, alongside diversification into solar solutions, and the Company will implement AI-driven Tender Intelligence Analytics to improve bid selection and win probability. Manufacturing operations are organised across four manufacturing sites at Nashik, Chakan, and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Maharashtra), supported by 18 warehouses; overall capacity utilisation across all plants stood at 59% for FY2026.
currentContext.mdna: India's consumer durable sector is projected to grow at an 11% CAGR in FY2027, supported by rising consumption, broader rural reach and growing global investment interest.|PLI Scheme allocation of ₹1,004 crore for FY2026-27 is expected to support capacity augmentation, local manufacturing and encourage new entrants in appliances.|Fan industry demand is being driven by a shift to BLDC motors and premium/smart models, rising urbanisation, El Nino-led hot summers, rising disposable income and rural electrification (first-time purchases).|Stricter BEE energy-efficiency and star-labelling norms are expected to elevate product standards and expedite replacement cycles, sustaining baseline demand.|India's professional lighting market is projected to grow from USD 354.33 million (2025) to USD 645.62 million by 2031 at a 10.52% CAGR, driven by smart-cities/urban infrastructure spend and demand for energy-efficient solutions.|Consumer lighting demand is supported by smart-home/IoT adoption and government programmes such as UJALA and PLI schemes anchoring supply-chain resilience.|Company's own exposure to weather-sensitive categories (coolers, fans) was partially offset by robust demand in core non-seasonal segments such as kitchen appliances.|India's continued infrastructure push, a rising aspirational middle class, and increasing penetration of branded electrical products in Tier II/III cities are cited as durable demand tailwinds.|Tariff barriers, supply chain reconfiguration, and commodity cost volatility (copper, aluminium) are flagged as headwinds affecting input costs and margins.|India GDP growth is projected at 6.9% for FY2026-27, with CPI inflation projected at 4.6%, supporting the broader consumption/investment backdrop for the business.|Professional lighting projects business continues to serve smart cities, stadiums, industrial complexes, and tunnels, described as demonstrating both technical capability and margin discipline.

risks.risk: Geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty (Middle East conflict, shifting trade policies)
risks.note: The AR flags high macroeconomic uncertainty, shifting trade policies and continuing fiscal challenges; geopolitical tensions in the Middle East add pressure, with disruptions in key shipping routes potentially raising freight costs and lead times, and volatility in crude oil and base metal prices (copper, aluminium) potentially raising input costs — directly relevant given Bajaj Electricals' exposure to copper/aluminium as commodity inputs.

The rupee hit an all-time low of approximately ₹95/USD during the year, driven by Middle East conflict volatility and FPI outflows; a weakening rupee accelerates domestic inflation by raising import costs (especially crude oil) and widens the trade deficit, which the Company is exposed to given import dependence in its supply chain.
Tariff-related trade disruptions and volatility in capital flows may intermittently affect exports and investor sentiment, per the MD&A macro outlook.

risks.risk: Supply-chain disruption from the West Asia conflict
risks.note: Supply-chain disruptions due to the West Asia conflict could tighten the availability of key inputs for downstream sectors, including plastics and aluminium — materials relevant to the Company's manufacturing base.

risks.risk: Import dependence and tightening regulatory/quality enforcement
risks.note: Import dependence exposes companies (including Bajaj Electricals) to currency fluctuations and supply disruptions from geopolitical conflicts, which may elevate input costs; separately, regulatory bodies such as the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) are strictly enforcing Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) norms, leading to increased product recalls and legal notices for non-compliant goods on e-commerce platforms.

Competition remains vigorous, intensified by established global and domestic players and low barriers to entry; aggressive pricing, frequent discounts and new product launches can weigh on margins over time.

The Consolidated Financial Analysis shows revenue, EBITDA, EBIT and PAT margins all declining year-on-year in FY26, with the Company moving from profit to loss at the PBT/PAT/Return-on-Net-Worth level — reflecting an operating-deleverage risk if demand softness persists.

risks.risk: Internal control gaps in automated systems
risks.note: The external Internal Auditor identified certain non-significant automated controls not configured during the year; these were mitigated by compensating manual controls, but represent a residual internal-control risk to monitor.

one-line thesis: Bajaj Electricals delivered a modest Q4FY26 with Lighting Solutions hitting record margins (8.5% annual) while Consumer Products faced losses due to delayed summer and intentional channel de-stocking. The strategic pivot from volume-push to demand-led sell-through is progressing, with inventory normalization expected to drive a rebound in FY27, though fan market share erosion due to BLDC gaps remains a critical near-term headwind.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Lighting +16% YoY (Q4), +9.5% YoY (FY26); Consumer Products mixed (Kitchen +30%, Fans/Coolers degrowth). EBITDA/Margin: Lighting annual EBIT margin 8.5% (record); Consumer Products reported loss due to operating deleverage. PAT: Not explicitly quantified in transcript but pressured by Consumer vertical loss and one-offs. Order Book: Wires category showing robust immediate traction post-Feb launch. Net Debt: Negative working capital position; INR 934 Cr cash on hand. One-offs: Exceptional items/write-offs addressed in FY26; management indicates most issues traced and resolved.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Intent to grow ahead of market (mid-single digit industry avg). Margin: Lighting EBIT likely stable as gains reinvested for growth; Consumer targetting industry avg 6-9% EBIT over medium term. Order Inflow: Strong in Wires/Switchgears. Capex: Substantial reduction in FY27/FY28 (<50% of past levels), focused on mould replacement and innovation.
order book & pipeline: Wires category launched in Feb FY26 seeing immediate robust orders; Professional and Consumer Lighting trade growing; No specific numeric order book value provided.
segment / subsidiary detail: Lighting Solutions: 16% Q4 revenue growth, 8.7% Q4 EBIT margin, 8.5% annual EBIT margin. Consumer Products: Kitchen appliances +30% growth; Fans and Coolers negative due to delayed summer and high channel inventory; Irons/Water Heaters modest growth. Wires: New entry with strong market response.
growth verticals / optionality: Wires category as new growth driver; Bridging BLDC fan technology gap to recover market share; Premiumization in Lighting; Expansion in Professional Lighting.
margins & cost dynamics: Lighting margins supported by premium mix; Consumer margins pressured by war-related inflation (partially passed via 3-10% price hikes) and inability to fully pass on costs due to demand uncertainty; Operating deleverage in Consumer vertical due to volume drop.
capex / expansion: FY27/FY28 capex plan: <50% of historical intensity; primarily for mould replacement and specific innovations rather than capacity expansion.
capital allocation: Dividend: INR 3/share (150% of face value) recommended for FY26; Cash flow positive (INR 400 Cr operating cash flow in Q4); Focus on brand building and innovation spend in next 12 months.
risks & watch-items: Delayed/patchy summer season impacting fans/coolers; War-geopolitical input cost inflation; Market share loss in Fans due to BLDC technology gap; Demand uncertainty limiting price pass-through.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Transparent about Consumer Products struggles; Confident in Lighting trajectory; Emphasis on 'cultural change' and sustainable profitability over volume push.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly stated they will reinvest Lighting margin gains to accelerate growth rather than bottom-line expansion; Fan segment weakness specifically tied to lack of competitive BLDC offerings vs. traditional induction strength; Inventory correction in coolers still ongoing but deemed non-material for full year.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Input cost inflation and demand uncertainty limiting price pass-through | Competitors with lower pricing power | loser | Med | Bajaj's brand strength allows partial pass-through (3-10%), squeezing weaker players. |
| Gap in BLDC fan technology causing market share loss | Havells India; Crompton Greaves | beneficiary | High | Peers with stronger BLDC portfolios are capturing the growing energy-efficient fan segment where Bajaj is weak. |
| Channel inventory correction creating short-term pain | Bajaj Electricals Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Once inventory normalizes (expected by FY27), sell-through data should reflect healthier demand without channel stuffing distortions. |

themes.title: Consumer durables, cooling & electricals
themes.need: Rising incomes, electrification and a record cooling season drive consumer-electricals and appliances - HAVELLS/VOLTAS/BLUESTARCO/SYMPHONY/ORIENTELEC on cooling & electricals; TTKPRESTIG/STOVEKRAFT/BAJAJELEC/EUREKAFORB on kitchen/home; CROMPTON-tier fans & pumps; premiumization + GST 2.0 + summer demand expand the organized share. Q1FY27's small-cap read: SONAMLTD grew revenue 75.6% YoY to INR 66.57cr on a cheap raw-material inventory position taken 6-7 months in advance while selling prices rose - management explicitly called the 75% print non-repeatable and guided FY27 to 25-30% with a Q2 floor of INR 40-50cr - and is pivoting from volume to INR 5,000-15,000 value clocks with capacity utilisation still only 60-70%.
themes.driver: Summer cooling demand; GST 2.0 price cuts; festive restocking; commodity-cost tailwind on margins; premiumization/ASP mix shift.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Bajaj Electricals Limited is a fast-moving electrical goods (FMEG) company with a legacy spanning over eight decades, operating across Consumer Products (fans, home and kitchen appliances, cooking solutions and grooming products) and Lighting Solutions (addressing both consumer and professional applications). With the addition of switchgears and wires under the Bajaj Secura brand, and strategic expansion into solar solutions, the Company has broadened its footprint within the electrical ecosystem. It sells through a multi-brand, 'house of brands' portfolio (Bajaj, Morphy Richards, Nirlep) to millions of consumers pan-India.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's consumer durable sector is projected to grow at an 11% CAGR in FY2027, supported by rising consumption, broader rural reach and growing global investment interest.
- PLI Scheme allocation of ₹1,004 crore for FY2026-27 is expected to support capacity augmentation, local manufacturing and encourage new entrants in appliances.
- Fan industry demand is being driven by a shift to BLDC motors and premium/smart models, rising urbanisation, El Nino-led hot summers, rising disposable income and rural electrification (first-time purchases).
- Stricter BEE energy-efficiency and star-labelling norms are expected to elevate product standards and expedite replacement cycles, sustaining baseline demand.
- India's professional lighting market is projected to grow from USD 354.33 million (2025) to USD 645.62 million by 2031 at a 10.52% CAGR, driven by smart-cities/urban infrastructure spend and demand for energy-efficient solutions.
- Consumer lighting demand is supported by smart-home/IoT adoption and government programmes such as UJALA and PLI schemes anchoring supply-chain resilience.
- Company's own exposure to weather-sensitive categories (coolers, fans) was partially offset by robust demand in core non-seasonal segments such as kitchen appliances.
- India's continued infrastructure push, a rising aspirational middle class, and increasing penetration of branded electrical products in Tier II/III cities are cited as durable demand tailwinds.
- Tariff barriers, supply chain reconfiguration, and commodity cost volatility (copper, aluminium) are flagged as headwinds affecting input costs and margins.
- India GDP growth is projected at 6.9% for FY2026-27, with CPI inflation projected at 4.6%, supporting the broader consumption/investment backdrop for the business.
- Professional lighting projects business continues to serve smart cities, stadiums, industrial complexes, and tunnels, described as demonstrating both technical capability and margin discipline.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Lighting margins supported by premium mix; Consumer margins pressured by war-related inflation (partially passed via 3-10% price hikes) and inability to fully pass on costs due to demand uncertainty; Operating deleverage in Consumer vertical due to volume drop.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Dividend: INR 3/share (150% of face value) recommended for FY26; Cash flow positive (INR 400 Cr operating cash flow in Q4); Focus on brand building and innovation spend in next 12 months.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company forayed into the switchgear segment with the launch of the BAJAJ SECURA brand (switchgear and wires), described as a strategic expansion of the lighting solutions business that extends the Company's generational expertise into a new category. The Company broadened its international footprint in FY2026 through targeted market initiatives: in Sri Lanka it introduced new appliance categories and strengthened the Morphy Richards presence through its established partner; in Nepal it implemented DMDC-based distribution for ceiling fans while consolidating appliance sales; in Dubai efforts focused on re-export partners with a consistent monthly push to grow market share in the ceiling fan segment. Looking to FY2027, the Professional Lighting business plans to strengthen its competitive edge through R&D and digital integration, with an emphasis on ultra-efficient solutions that reduce carbon footprints; growth efforts will be pursued across infrastructure, sports, office spaces and data centres, alongside diversification into solar solutions, and the Company will implement AI-driven Tender Intelligence Analytics to improve bid selection and win probability. Manufacturing operations are organised across four manufacturing sites at Nashik, Chakan, and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Maharashtra), supported by 18 warehouses; overall capacity utilisation across all plants stood at 59% for FY2026.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; Transparent about Consumer Products struggles; Confident in Lighting trajectory; Emphasis on 'cultural change' and sustainable profitability over volume push.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Legacy spanning over eight decades as a household FMEG name and vital pillar of the Bajaj Group
- Pan-India distribution scale: 850+ distributors (Board's overview) / 2,000+ channel partners (MD&CEO message), nearly 2,00,000+ retail outlets, and 770+/778 consumer care centres reaching 19,000 pin codes
- Multi-brand 'house of brands' portfolio (Bajaj, Morphy Richards, Nirlep) each anchored in a distinct value proposition, spanning the full price spectrum
- Full brand ownership of Morphy Richards (post-acquisition) enabling sharper premiumisation and margin control versus the prior licensing arrangement
- Engineering depth in professional lighting projects (smart cities, stadiums, industrial complexes, tunnels) described by the MD & CEO as a real competitive moat
- Digital enablement across the trade network (DMS, Sarathi App, DSO App, Power BI) strengthening distributor governance and transparency

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Delayed/patchy summer season impacting fans/coolers; War-geopolitical input cost inflation; Market share loss in Fans due to BLDC technology gap; Demand uncertainty limiting price pass-through.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly stated they will reinvest Lighting margin gains to accelerate growth rather than bottom-line expansion; Fan segment weakness specifically tied to lack of competitive BLDC offerings vs. traditional induction strength; Inventory correction in coolers still ongoing but deemed non-material for full year.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Accelerating domestic sourcing, localising critical components, and reducing single-country dependencies in response to tariff and geopolitical supply-chain risk.
- Operating a clear two-brand strategy: the BAJAJ brand (refreshed identity) serves mass and aspirational segments, while the fully-owned Morphy Richards addresses the upper mid-market and premium lifestyle segment.
- Accelerating premiumisation — launching upgraded, energy-efficient and higher-value SKUs (400+ new SKUs across consumer products and lighting in recent years) and moving the product mix upward while defending …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Input cost inflation and demand uncertainty limiting price pass-through | Competitors with lower pricing power | loser | Med | Bajaj's brand strength allows partial pass-through (3-10%), squeezing weaker players. |
| Gap in BLDC fan technology causing market share loss | Havells India; Crompton Greaves | beneficiary | High | Peers with stronger BLDC portfolios are capturing the growing energy-efficient fan segment where Bajaj is weak. |
| Channel inventory correction creating short-term pain | Bajaj Electricals Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Once inventory normalizes (expected by FY27), sell-through data should reflect healthier demand without channel stuffing distortions. |
